Björner–Wachs §7 and the referenced Armstrong orbit-space theorem
correctness.rationale: The signed partitions are the intersection lattice of the type-B arrangement, so the geometric-lattice proper-part theorem makes its realization simply connected. A coordinate transposition fixes the proper rank-two partition with its two coordinates in the zero block. Armstrong's quotient formula applies to this simply connected finite complex with finite group action and kills every generating transposition. The rank-preserving action identifies no distinct points within any closed simplex: barycentric coefficients at each rank must agree. Thus orbit cells have the oriented face-deletion boundary stated in the record; this is not a claim that the quotient is an abstract simplicial complex. I rebuilt the lattice from joins of its 25 arrangement atoms, merging inconsistent signed components into the zero block; rebuilt all flags and their unsigned permutation orbits; and checked the chain compositions. Ordinary flag counts are 646,7910,20720,14400, and orbit cell counts are 37,242,471,274. Integral diagonalization of each boundary separately produced only unit nonzero factors, with ranks 36,206,265. Hence each image is saturated in the whole chain group and in the next kernel, and integral homology ranks are 1,0,0,9. Simple connectivity and Hurewicz give representatives for a basis of H3; the wedge map is a homology equivalence between simply connected CW complexes, hence a homotopy equivalence.
residual_risks: Exact integral calculation at rank five only; the quotient is neither an equivariant splitting of the cover nor a Borel construction.

Björner–Wachs labeled results, Henderson's character results and Arone's type-A quotient result
value.rationale: The pure-coordinate subgroup is canonical and retains sign information; its nonfree action makes the actual quotient a different object from the labeled complex. The answer rules out lower integral torsion and nontrivial fundamental group as well as giving the exact sphere number. This is a useful concrete test case for extending partition-complex quotient results to signed posets; it is not just a rational invariant or a group-order calculation.
residual_risks: Rank-specific; no inference about all ranks, other subgroups, or a full wreath-product quotient.
